# Proverbs 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A wise child accepts a father's correction, but a mocker refuses to hear anyone's rebuke.

**2** The good things a person says come back to feed them, but what the treacherous crave is violence.

**3** Watch your words and you protect your life. Talk without thinking, and you'll destroy yourself.

**4** A lazy person wants everything but gets nothing. A hard worker gets everything they need and more.

**5** A righteous person hates dishonesty, but the wicked stink of shame and disgrace.

**6** Righteousness stands guard over those who live honestly, but wickedness brings down the sinner.

**7** Some people pretend to be rich but have nothing; others pretend to be poor but are actually wealthy.

**8** A rich person's wealth can buy their way out of danger, but a poor person never even hears a ransom demand.

**9** The life of a righteous person shines brightly, but the wicked person's lamp will be snuffed out.

**10** Arrogance only starts fights. Wisdom shows up in those who are willing to take advice.

**11** Easy money disappears fast, but money earned bit by bit grows over time.

**12** When you keep hoping and nothing happens, it makes your heart sick. But when what you've longed for finally arrives — it's like a tree of life.

**13** Ignore good advice and it will cost you. Respect wise instruction and you'll be rewarded.

**14** What a wise person teaches is a life-giving spring — it can steer you away from deadly traps.

**15** Good judgment earns people's respect, but the road of the dishonest is hard and unforgiving.

**16** A smart person thinks before they act, but a fool puts their foolishness on full display.

**17** An unreliable messenger creates problems, but a trustworthy one brings solutions.

**18** Ignore correction and you'll end up broke and embarrassed. Accept it and you'll be respected.

**19** Getting what you've wanted feels wonderful — but fools refuse to give up evil to get it.

**20** Spend time with wise people and you'll become wise. Hang around fools and you'll pay the price.

**21** Trouble chases down sinners, but good things find their way to the righteous.

**22** A good person leaves wealth that lasts for generations, but what the wicked accumulate ends up in the hands of the righteous.

**23** Even unworked land belonging to the poor could produce a lot of food — but injustice sweeps it all away.

**24** If you refuse to discipline your child, you don't really love them. If you love them, you'll correct them early.

**25** The righteous eat until they're satisfied, but the wicked go hungry.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **13:7**: This is about pretense — people who fake wealth they don't have, and people who hide wealth they do have. Both are performing.

- **13:12**: This is one of the realest things ever written. Long-delayed hope doesn't just disappoint — it can make you physically ill. But fulfillment? Pure life.

- **13:20**: You become like the people you spend the most time with. It's that simple and that important.

— PNEUMA
